repo.name: chakra-ui
repo.description: Chakra UI is a component system for building SaaS products with speed ⚡️

readme.summary: The README covers branding and installation well but defers almost all practical documentation to an external website, leaving the README itself nearly useless as a standalone reference.
readme.top_issue: Usage section contains only a link to external docs with no inline quick-start example or code snippet showing basic component usage.

common_complaints: Date/Date Range Picker mobile responsiveness and styling issues
Recipe and styling definitions not matching documentation behavior
praise_themes: Well-documented issue reports with reproduction links
sentiment.summary: Active but stretched: project maintains reasonable closure rate (6 closed vs 5 open) but several recent issues receive no maintainer comments and one issue carries a 'stale' label, suggesting maintenance capacity constraints.

red_flags: Some responses are brief and could be more detailed for complex issues
One response mentions that v2 is no longer maintained, which might discourage users from upgrading
communication.summary: The maintainer responses are generally helpful and clear, showing patience with repeated questions and welcoming new contributors. However, they could benefit from more technical depth in some explanations.

concerns: Zero commits in past 6 months despite one recent commit today
32 open issues with no resolution activity in past 6 months
No merged PRs in past 6 months
Zero active contributors in past 6 months
Unknown last release date - unclear if releases are being published
positive_signals: Very recent commit on 2026-03-16 indicates some activity
No open PRs - no stalled work in progress
maintenance.summary: Package appears stale with sporadic maintenance; recent commit suggests occasional attention but lack of issue resolution, PR activity, and active contributors over 6 months indicates minimal ongoing maintenance.

governance.summary: The documentation outlines a clear decision-making process and path for contributors to become maintainers, indicating multiple people with merge rights. However, there is no explicit succession plan in place.
